headline: The ceasefire died, the rally lived: Brent settled at $106.65 — the highest since Sept 15 — as the US session dismissed Trump's energy truce and bought the war premium back, while DXY printed a 1.5-year high near ~102.4 on crude plus hawkish Hammack.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: DXY printed a 1.5-year high near ~102.4 into NY close — the war bid and the rate bid stacked: a ~2% oil surge plus hawkish Hammack. December hike odds sit ~75–85% depending on the feed.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the dollar rallied to its strongest since April 2025 (up +0.37%) on two fuels at once — crude's ~2% surge, which markets read as inflation risk, and Cleveland Fed President Hammack saying inflation pressures are 'broad-based, not concentrated' and that policy must stay restrictive. Thin holiday liquidity (US bonds closed for Columbus Day, Tokyo shut) magnified the move. Thread: the hawkish hold is in week five; this morning the prop was the rate bid alone at ~102.2. What it means: confirms the prior thesis — the dollar now carries both the war bid and the rate bid. Treat the tape with respect, not reverence: holiday thinness cut both ways.
chapters.fx: What to watch: CPI Wednesday 7:30am CT — consensus ~3.6% y/y, core m/m ~0.2%, core y/y ~2.5%. A soft core deflates the rate leg and squeezes crowded dollar longs; a hot core revives the October hike (~19–22% priced). Warsh speaks Thursday 10:30pm CT, the last Fed voice before the Oct 17 blackout.
numbers: US 10Y 5.24% Fri (bonds closed Mon for holiday)
CPI Wed 7:30am CT (cons 3.6% y/y; core m/m 0.2%)

scenarios.base: The hawkish hold rides into CPI week; crowded dollar longs make the dollar jumpy but bid.
scenarios.bull: Hot CPI (core 0.3%+) revives the October hike — DXY breaks out above the 1.5-year high.
scenarios.bear: Soft core (0.2% or below) knocks the rate leg out and crowded longs squeeze — DXY gives back a percent.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: EUR/USD broke to 1.1155–1.116, a 17-month low — the morning's 'steadied' read died by midday: a 175bp US–Bund gap on one side, France's 152bp spread on the other.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the euro gave up its early bounce and fell to a 17-month low (down 0.39%), holding just above October's 1.1163 print as the dollar rallied across the board. ECB's Stournaras pushed back: a hike this month is less likely than December (Oct 29 odds ~12%), and France's OAT–Bund spread spiked to 152bp — widest since 2011 — ahead of Tuesday's budget plenary. Thread: this morning we had it steady at ~1.12 with the Oct 5 1.1161 low holding; the US session broke the steadiness, not the line. What it means: breaks the morning's steadiness thesis — the euro is squeezed from both ends: the US–German 10Y gap at 175bp on the dollar side, fiscal stress on its own side, and an ECB that can't hike fast without risking a bond-market accident.
chapters.fx: What to watch: French budget plenary Tuesday 3:00am CT — the spread is now a real-time input for EUR/USD; German ZEW Tuesday 4:00am CT (expected 40.5 vs 37.3); 1.1161 is the line — a close below confirms the breakdown; Wednesday's CPI reprices the dollar side.
numbers: ECB Oct 29 hike ~12%; next hike not fully priced until Feb
EUR down 3.18% over the past month

scenarios.base: EUR/USD grinds 1.1150–1.1250 into CPI; Tuesday's plenary decides whether the French spread is the story or just the backdrop.
scenarios.bull: Clean French plenary plus soft US CPI — crowded EUR shorts squeeze and the pair lifts back over 1.1250.
scenarios.bear: Spread re-widens past 152bp or hot CPI — 1.1161 breaks and 1.1100 comes into view.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: Sterling sat the session out at ~$1.321 — down 0.19% in the dollar's slipstream, but near 16-month highs against the euro; the hawkish-BoE floor held.
chapters.meaning: What changed: almost nothing — GBP/USD slipped 0.19% to ~1.3209 while EUR/GBP hovered at 16-month lows (~0.8446): the euro's pain, not sterling's. Thread: the November 5 hike stays ~86% priced, Bailey speaks four times this week starting Wednesday, and UK GDP lands Thursday (forecast −0.1% m/m). What it means: confirms the prior thesis — sterling is the best of the European losers, floored by the BoE's hawkish hold while the euro drowns.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Bailey's four appearances — Wed 12:30am CT, Thu 2:30am CT, Thu 9:00pm CT (the big one, post-data), Sat 1:45am CT; UK GDP Thursday 1:00am CT (fcst −0.1% m/m) is the growth counterpoint to the hike case.

scenarios.base: Sterling drifts sideways, anchored by the hike case into Bailey's Thursday speech.
scenarios.bull: Soft US CPI knocks the dollar leg out — cable back over $1.33.
scenarios.bear: Weak UK GDP Thursday dents the hike case — EUR/GBP relents and cable slips.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: USD/JPY rose to ~158.64 (+0.21%), a two-week high — higher crude weighed on the yen and the rate gap did the rest; intervention talk caps the top.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the yen fell to a two-week low as Monday's ~2% crude jump (a tax on Japan, which imports 90%+ of its energy) stacked onto the rate gap; the pair held below the weekend high of 158.75 with Tokyo shut for the holiday. Thread: the morning had it at ~158.2 with the rate gap beating the fear bid; the gap won harder by the close. What it means: confirms the thesis — with the oil fade dead, the rate-gap pull toward 159–160 is the dominant force and intervention risk is the only ceiling.
chapters.fx: What to watch: crude holding above ~$105 — the pain line for Japan's import bill; Friday's CFTC update on yen longs (62,325 last week); Wednesday's CPI, which reprices the Fed side of the gap; BoJ Oct 29–30 (this month's hike odds ~9%).

scenarios.base: USD/JPY consolidates 158–159 into CPI; the gap pulls, intervention talk caps.
scenarios.bull: Hot CPI revives October hike talk — the top of the range gives way toward 160.
scenarios.bear: A verified ceasefire or soft CPI — the rate gap narrows and the pair slips back under 157.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: USD/CHF rose 0.54% to ~0.8347 — the day's biggest dollar move: fear returned with the oil surge, but the dollar won both legs.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the haven bid came back — and the franc still fell, because the dollar's own haven-plus-rate bid was stronger: USD/CHF's +0.54% was the largest USD gain of the day. Thread: this morning the franc slept at 0.8306 on the oil fade; the afternoon's escalation re-armed fear and the franc lost anyway. What it means: partially breaks the morning's flat-franc read — fear is real again, but it's expressing through the dollar, not the franc; EUR/CHF at 0.9311 shows the French stress transmitting only lightly so far.
chapters.fx: What to watch: fresh escalation headlines — the only thing that re-prices the franc; Schlegel speaks Wednesday 11:30pm CT; EUR/CHF as the contagion gauge (a sharp drop means France is spreading).
numbers: USD/CHF ~0.8347 (+0.54%; biggest USD move of the day)

scenarios.base: The franc drifts with fear headlines; the dollar leg dominates unless escalation surprises.
scenarios.bull: A verified supply shock — the haven bid finally finds the franc and USD/CHF drops.
scenarios.bear: De-escalation confirmed — the fear premium clears and USD/CHF grinds higher.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: AUD/USD slipped to ~0.6959 (−0.36%) — the risk proxy sagged into tonight's RBA minutes at 7:30pm CT, the first real domestic input of the week.
chapters.meaning: What changed: a soft drift, not a break — the Aussie fell with the risk proxies as oil's surge lifted the dollar; the morning's flat read bent but didn't break. Thread: the RBA hiked on Sep 29 to 4.60% but Bullock struck a dovish-leaning tone after; tonight's minutes show whether the tightening bias survived. Westpac expects one more hike by year-end; CBA says the hurdle is higher now. What it means: the risk-proxy read stays parked — tonight's minutes are the unlock, with Australia jobs Thursday as the next swing factor.
chapters.fx: What to watch: RBA minutes tonight 7:30pm CT — any tightening-bias lean supports the AUD's best-in-G10 policy case; Australia jobs Thursday (unemployment expected 4.6%, highest since late 2021); China CPI Tuesday 8:30pm CT.
numbers: RBA minutes tonight 7:30pm CT (Sep 29 hike to 4.60%)

scenarios.base: Minutes read hawkish-but-patient; AUD consolidates ~0.695 into Wednesday.
scenarios.bull: Minutes lean hawkish and AU jobs beat — the best-in-G10 policy case re-rates.
scenarios.bear: Minutes sound done hiking — the policy edge erodes and AUD underperforms the risk proxies.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: USD/CAD held at ~1.4282 (+0.19%) — the oil surge ($106.65 Brent) should have been the loonie's moment; instead the 161bp gap and a raging dollar kept it pinned near 18-month lows.
chapters.meaning: What changed: oil's hand strengthened — Brent settled at $106.65, the highest since Sept 15 — but the tug-of-war tilted back to the dollar: USD/CAD barely moved from the 18-month lows. Thread: this morning the fade was thinning the oil offset; by the close the offset was back and the loonie still couldn't rally — the rate gap never blinked. What it means: confirms the tug-of-war thesis but shifts the lesson — the oil offset is real, yet it's losing to a 161bp gap and a 1.5-year-high dollar; the loonie needs the gap to narrow, not just crude to rise.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Macklem speaks Wednesday 1:05am CT; BoC Oct 28 (hike ~25% priced — the jobs shock killed the old hawkish-BoC thesis); Canada CPI Oct 21; WTI ~$93.8 is the real terms-of-trade read for Canada.

scenarios.base: Tug-of-war holds; USD/CAD consolidates 1.42–1.43 into the BoC.
scenarios.bull: Soft US CPI narrows the gap — the oil offset finally bites and the loonie firms.
scenarios.bear: Hot CPI widens the gap — 18-month lows break toward 1.44.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The quietest chapter again — ~$0.5587, down with the dollar's tide; the RBNZ's Oct 28 two-way bet is still the only thing on the calendar.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing — the kiwi drifted with the risk proxies, softer by ~0.3% as the dollar rallied. Thread: the RBNZ sits at 2.75% with Oct 28 a genuine two-way bet (~50% priced, down from ~75%); NZ CPI lands Oct 21. What it means: thesis stands — this one drifts with risk sentiment into the RBNZ; the dollar's Monday was the whole story.
chapters.fx: What to watch: NZ CPI Oct 21 — the number that settles the two-way bet; tonight's RBA minutes for AUD spillover; Wednesday's US CPI for the dollar leg.

scenarios.base: NZD drifts with risk sentiment into the RBNZ decision.
scenarios.bull: RBNZ hikes Oct 28 after all — NZD re-rates higher.
scenarios.bear: RBNZ pauses and sounds done — NZD underperforms the commodity bloc.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: The fade died: Brent settled at $106.65 (+1.8%) — the highest since Sept 15 — after the US session called Trump's energy ceasefire unverified and the Gulf escalation owned the tape.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the complete round trip — crude jumped ~2% Monday morning (Brent $106.80 intraday) and settled at $106.65, up $6.45 (+6.4%) in three sessions. The ceasefire story collapsed: the Kremlin wouldn't confirm it, Zelensky said Russia kept striking energy facilities, and Kyiv's 60-day truce was rejected; meanwhile the Houthis' deadly Saturday strike on Riyadh's airport (13 killed, 300+ wounded), Sunday's second attack, Monday's intercepted ballistic missile toward Riyadh, and two tanker strikes near Oman and the Strait of Hormuz dominated. Russia's 300k-tonne diesel deal and partial export-ban lift barely registered. Thread: this morning we wrote 'priced the war, then sold it' at ~$103.4; the US session sold the fade and bought the war back. What it means: breaks the morning's premium thesis — Goldman now sees just over $20/bbl of geopolitical premium with December Brent at $90, and OPEC cut 2026 demand growth to 400k bpd. The ~$13 Brent–WTI spread stays the geopolitical-premium gauge: wide means the premium is shipping and geopolitics, not demand.
chapters.fx: What to watch: whether Moscow ever confirms the ceasefire (the market says no); Trump's decision on joining Saudi strikes; physical diesel cargoes (the deal's real test, not the press release); GoM restart figures (Shell, Chevron, BP restoring after Hurricane Isaias); the EIA weekly. Spread toward $15 = Hormuz risk back in force; toward $5 = premium truly unwinding.

scenarios.base: Brent holds $103–108; the market needs a verified supply shock or a verified ceasefire to leave this range.
scenarios.bull: Trump joins the Saudi campaign or a verified Hormuz disruption — Brent toward $110+, spread past $15.
scenarios.bear: Ceasefire confirmation or fast GoM restarts — Brent under $100, spread collapses toward $5.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Comex gold settled ~$4,166 (−0.6%) — the dollar leg beat the haven leg; the PBOC's 23rd straight month of buying is the quiet bid underneath.
chapters.meaning: What changed: gold gave back the morning's firmness — Comex settled down ~$26 (−0.6%) at ~$4,166 as DXY's rally to a 1.5-year high did the damage; spot ran ~$4,167–4,177 versus ~$4,206 this morning. Thread: the morning's two-engine read had the haven leg fading and the anti-dollar leg loading into CPI; the US session proved the dollar leg is the heavier engine. What it means: confirms the two-engine read — gold's haven bid couldn't outrun a surging dollar; Wednesday's CPI is still the deciding print.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Wednesday's CPI — soft core (0.2%) weakens the dollar leg and re-arms gold toward $4,300; hot core sends it back toward $4,000. PBOC reserves hit 77.47M oz in September (+740k oz) — the structural bid.
numbers: PBOC +740k oz in Sep (23rd straight month)

scenarios.base: Gold consolidates $4,100–4,300 into Wednesday's CPI; direction comes from the print.
scenarios.bull: CPI undershoots and hike bets collapse — gold breaks $4,300 and the anti-dollar trade broadens.
scenarios.bear: Hot CPI revives the October hike; real yields jump and gold slides back toward $4,000.
